title: Looking for feedback [ PokeTime - Browser idle game ]
author: Voiston44
selftext:
Hello everyone, a few days ago I asked for advice here on how to completely migrate my game from Vanilla JS to something more modern!



After a fair amount of tokens, testing, etc., the migration is complete, and the game is finally running in TypeScript/Vite/Svelte! We're talking about roughly 1.5 billion tokens to migrate everything, which luckily cost me around $20 thanks to Deepseek and a day when Composer 2.5 was 90% off on Cursor.



This is my first game, and I'm a complete beginner. The development was a bit chaotic; I started by copying and pasting from Gemini to Notepad++, The road has therefore been very long ! Despite the AI, I learned a lot working on this little project.



There's still work to be done, but I'm already playing it, and I think it's time to seek some outside feedback!



The core gameplay is simply that you have total stats for your account, which are incremented every second by your Pokémon. As you might have guessed, to get high stats and see the numbers climb, you need the strongest Pokémon possible. For this, you have, for example, a prestige system for each Pokémon. The account itself never prestiges, but each Pokémon has its own prestige level to become more powerful.



Pokémon have ultimate moves, abilities, there's a team synergy system, a collection system, and so on. I'll let you discover the game for yourself!



I like numbers, so I've added quite a few metrics to the UI.



The save file is 100% local, so be careful and back it up regularly.



Regarding your feedback:

Is the pacing good?

What do you think of the UI?

Did you easily understand all the features?

Is the optimization okay?



I would welcome any feedback that could improve my game, thank you!

Here the link : [https://poketime-idle.github.io/PokeTime/](https://poketime-idle.github.io/PokeTime/)

replies.author: RecursiveServitor

replies.author: Asleepius_Games
replies.body:
Protecting IP is more than protecting profits. If they see a product that is close enough to their IP and gets popular, They almost have to file against it. If not, it establishes to the courts that the IP can be used by anyone. 

Someone could say "Why am I getting sued when there are other products that use the IP and not been sued?". This is the reason why companies are so strict about protecting their IP. Look at the case of the pre-school that drew a mural of classic Disney characters. Sort of a happy ending there but a good example of why companies will sue products that seem like they shouldn't be an issue.

Pokemon is another beast still. They really want to make sure their creatures stay protected based on how much of a cash cow their cards and games are. Making bespoke games based on the IP they see as taking away from the value and uniqueness of pokemon. Printing cards is like printing cash for them, they wont just want anyone diluting that system. One reason I will never care about pokemon personally. If they had it their way, they wouldn't allow anyone to have anything close to a creature collection game.

comments.author: addictiveboi
comments.body:
I really like it! The style and everything is really cool. It looks great. A few things I noticed are:  
1. Some text is still in french even though most of it is in English, like certain text in the pokedex and the ultimate description for the pokemon.  
2. The UI extends beyond my browser window, horizontally, when I have the window a bit smaller. My screen isn't that big so it became a slight issue. I like idlers but I generally speaking like to have my window be fairly small so it doesn't distract me too much.  
3. I would lastly say, just my own preference would be if the UI was a bit simpler. I found that I was looking around and searching for things a lot with my eyes, and it became slightly straining.

Other than that I really like it and think it's cool. I would probably be careful with the Pokemon theme for the future though, since Nintendo are known to sue.

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body: For the point 2, Does this happen when you're in fullscreen mode or only in a resized window?

replies.author: addictiveboi
replies.body: Both actually. It seems like my window needs to be pretty wide and not very tall for it to work well for me.
